questions.q: Why does Jantsch say a mission matters more than goals or strategy?
a: It sustains you through the moments you feel like quitting
It is what convinces investors to fund your business
It is what makes your advertising easier to remember
It is what allows you to charge higher prices
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a mission carries you past roadblocks, while ambitions like market leadership will not.

questions.q: What makes a customer a champion?
a: They love your product and tell all their friends about it
They buy from you once and never return
They compare your prices with competitors before buying
They sign up for your newsletter but never purchase
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines champions as repeat customers who love your products so much that they keep recommending you to friends.

questions.q: According to the summary, who are a business's best new customers?
a: Its existing customers, treated exceptionally well
Its largest competitors' unhappy customers
Its newest prospects from paid advertising
Its suppliers and local business partners
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues that your best new customers are your old ones, because good service turns clients into champions.

questions.q: What does the book mean by saying that if you are not online, you do not exist?
a: Small businesses must pick an online channel and start creating
Every business must sell physical products through a website
Only social media advertising can reach new customers today
A business without a blog cannot build customer trust
questions.why: Lesson 3 says offline marketing still works in some industries, but you must choose one online channel and begin.

questions.q: What should a company's mission be like?
a: Idealistic in tone and aimed at a broader good
Specific about revenue targets and market share
Focused on beating the nearest competitor
Simple enough to fit on a business card
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a mission should lean toward idealism and serve others, like treating customers' homes as your own.
